corridor_responsibilities.duty: Steward owns artillery death. Durin contributes only when actual target selection permits. Neither ground blocking nor a retreat is credited as stopping the flying enemy or removing born shells.
Midnight destroys the eastern upper restraint while alternating actual hostile targets. Returning Midnight destroys the western upper restraint. Observe safe arrival.

Durin destroys the eastern lower restraint. Cardigan intercepts officers after their approach to the civilian; blocking does not erase earlier protected-target attacks. Returning Durin destroys the western lower restraint.
Fang holds the upper inner lane. Midnight supplies available opening crossfire. Returning Durin and subsequently repositioned Steward must kill retained armor before Fang's two slots overflow.
Friston holds the lower inner lane. Both medics support him. Eastern approach damage and returning arts output must prevent a fourth simultaneous held enemy.
Midnight remains the upper outer interceptor through the final assigned officer. Ansel's extended healing windows explicitly support this duty.
Cardigan holds the lower outer lane at column 4. Self-heals sustain ordinary pressure and eligible artillery impacts; his ordinary range does not reach the eastern restraint.

formation_transitions.transition: Complete the eight-unit formation. Ansel supplements inner and Durin recovery; Hibiscus retains Steward recovery.

Return Midnight west after 2101 frames to destroy the remaining upper restraint.

revised_operational_plans.tactical_thesis: Use four lane holders, two medics and two arts attackers. Midnight supplies opening crossfire; Cardigan replaces the fragile lower outer opening. Establish eastern artillery coverage, clear both eastern civilian restraints, then rotate Durin into direct inner-lane clearance. This is an unverified full-stage hypothesis, with explicit medical and clearance gates; it is not a demonstrated winning plan.
